# Ben Stewart

> I run engineering teams working out AI in real time. Field reports on what's working, what's breaking and what the data says, in plain English.

Ben Stewart is VP of Engineering at Skyscanner, based in Glasgow. He writes field reports about leading engineering teams through AI: what is working, what is breaking and what the data says.

## Start here

- [What Level Does This Task Deserve?](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/what-level-does-this-task-deserve): Two questions I ask before I hand anything to AI. What it costs if the output is wrong, and whether I can check it.
- [The £3 Question](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/the-three-pound-question): Most AI tools wait to be asked. Clawdbot messages you first, which exposed the gap between reactive AI you pick up and proactive AI that acts.
- [Sustainable Pace Just Got Faster](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/sustainable): Speed won. AI compressed the cycle so hard that last year's fast is slow and teams are burning out. Substitute work, don't add it.
- [AI Made Writing Free. That Was Supposed to Be Good News.](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/ai-made-writing-free): AI made writing free, so the cost moved from the writer's time to the reader's brain. Here's how to take responsibility for what you send.
- [Ralph Isn't the Point. The PRD Is.](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/ralph-isnt-the-point): Ralph runs AI coding tools in a loop against a PRD. It works, though the PRD is the real work. Specifying clearly is the skill that lasts.
- [I Built a System Where AI Agents Argue About Strategy](https://www.benstewart.ai/posts/multi-agent-ai-strategy): Six AI personas argue about a strategy, then a 'So What?' gate forces an action. The system I use to stress-test my thinking, prompt included.
